resources.string: The thin extension covers much of the air-facing surface and shortens the diffusion path.
The flattened nucleus lies in a slightly thicker region of the cell.
These organelles store surfactant before release into the lining fluid.
Type II cells release surfactant here, helping lower surface tension at the air–liquid interface.
Coordinated ciliary beating moves mucus along the larger airways.
The cilia project from the surface that faces the airway lumen.
The widened apical region stores granules containing mucins that help form mucus.
The lower part of the cell is narrower than its granule-rich apex.
Club cells have a rounded apical profile without motile cilia.
The apical granules contain secretory products that contribute to the bronchiolar lining.
Neighboring podocyte foot processes interdigitate, leaving filtration slits between them.
This shared matrix lies between the capillary endothelium and podocyte foot processes.
Larger branches extend from the cell body and divide into foot processes.
Mesangial cells sit between capillary loops, not along the continuous filtration surface.
Cell processes and surrounding matrix support the capillary loops.
Dense microvilli enlarge the luminal surface available for reabsorption.
Mitochondria supply energy for active transport across the epithelium.
Distal tubular cells lack the dense brush border seen in the proximal tubule.
Membrane folds expand the surface facing the surrounding interstitium.
Vasopressin regulates the amount of aquaporin-2 at this surface.
Principal cells participate in water and electrolyte regulation in the collecting duct.
In type A intercalated cells, this pump moves protons into the duct lumen.
Intercalated cells contain many mitochondria that support active transport.
This superficial urothelial cell can flatten as the urinary tract stretches.
The apical membrane and cell junctions help separate urine from underlying tissue.
Pressure difference = 2 × surface tension ÷ radius (single spherical interface).
An ideal spherical interface, not a lung model. It omits tissue elasticity and interactions between alveoli. Not a breathing pressure or ventilator setting.
Same surface tension. Radius %1$s μm: %2$s Pa. Double radius %3$s μm: %4$s Pa.
A schematic of the whole filtration barrier: capillary endothelium, shared basement membrane and podocyte slits. Layers are not to scale. This does not estimate filtration rate.
